title: Add 10 Long Vrat Kathas with Narration to Vrat Katha Section

requirements.text: Add 10 complete, long-form Vrat Kathas in Hindi to the static data file `frontend/src/lib/kathaData.ts` under the `vrat` category. The 10 kathas must include: (1) Ekadashi Vrat Katha, (2) Solah Somvar Vrat Katha, (3) Mangalwar (Mangalvar) Vrat Katha, (4) Sukrwar (Shukravar) Vrat Katha, (5) Karva Chauth Vrat Katha, (6) Santoshi Mata Vrat Katha, (7) Pradosh Vrat Katha, (8) Navratri Vrat Katha, (9) Satyanarayan Vrat Katha, (10) Hartalika Teej Vrat Katha. Each katha must have a full Hindi text of significant length (at minimum 400–600 words of narrative content), a meaningful title in Hindi and English, associated deity name, and the `vrat` category tag.

quotes: add only 10 long vrat katha on ekadashi solah somvar mangalwar sukrwar ekadashi krva chauth and other

acceptanceCriteria: Exactly 10 Vrat Katha entries exist in the static data with category 'vrat'
Each katha includes: Ekadashi, Solah Somvar, Mangalwar, Sukrwar, Karva Chauth, Santoshi Mata, Pradosh, Navratri, Satyanarayan, Hartalika Teej
Each katha's Hindi text is long-form (400+ words of narrative)
Each katha has a title, deity, and category field populated

requirements.text: Ensure the Kathayen listing page (`frontend/src/pages/Kathayen.tsx`) correctly displays all 10 Vrat Kathas when the 'vrat' category tab is selected. The section must not appear empty — use the static data from `kathaData.ts` as the primary or fallback source so content always renders even without a backend response.

quotes: No there nothing in vrat katha section

acceptanceCriteria: Vrat Katha tab/filter shows exactly 10 katha cards
Content renders from static fallback even if the backend returns no data
Each card shows the correct title, deity, and a Hindi text preview

requirements.text: Add audio narration controls to the Katha detail page (`frontend/src/pages/KathaDetail.tsx`) for Vrat Kathas. Use the existing `useSpeechNarration` hook (`frontend/src/hooks/useSpeechNarration.ts`) to implement Play, Pause, Resume, and Stop buttons. The narration must read the full Hindi text aloud using the Web Speech API with Hindi (`hi-IN`) voice preference. Show narration controls prominently near the top of the katha content. Display current narration state (playing / paused / stopped) visually.
acceptanceCriteria: Play button starts reading the katha text aloud in Hindi
Pause button pauses mid-narration and Resume resumes from the same position
Narration controls are visible for all Vrat Kathas on the detail page
Active narration state (playing/paused) is reflected in button styling
Narration uses hi-IN voice preference via the useSpeechNarration hook

requirements.text: Seed the backend (`backend/main.mo`) with the same 10 Vrat Kathas so they persist in canister state. Each entry must include title, Hindi text body, deity, and category `vrat`. Update the migration file (`backend/migration.mo`) if the current state schema change requires it to preserve existing data while adding the new vrat katha entries.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend actor contains 10 seeded Vrat Katha records with category 'vrat'
Existing data (temples, community posts, jap counters, other kathas) is not lost after upgrade
Each backend katha record has title, text, deity, and category fields populated

constraints: Do not remove or modify any existing Katha entries (Ramayan, Mahabharat chapters, etc.)
Do not edit files under frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, or frontend/src/components/ui
Narration must use the existing useSpeechNarration hook — do not reimplement Web Speech API logic
All user-facing text labels for narration controls must be in English
nonGoals: Adding Ramayan or Krishna Leela content in this build
Adding any paid/premium audio files or external TTS services
Building a custom audio player UI beyond play/pause/resume/stop controls
Adding new backend routes or changing the Katha data schema
